questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Three months ago, she underwent heart transplantation for restrictive cardiomyopathy and was started on transplant rejection prophylaxis. Her pulse is 76/min and her blood pressure is 148/82 mm Hg. Physical examination shows an enlargement of the gum tissue. There is a well-healed scar on her chest. Serum studies show hyperlipidemia. The physician recommends removing a drug that decreases T cell activation by inhibiting the transcription of interleukin-2 from the patient's treatment regimen and replacing it with a different medication. Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause of the adverse effects seen in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cyclosporine
  • In addition to hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gingival hyperplasia seen in this patient, other adverse effects of this medication include hirsutism, nephrotoxicity, and neurotoxicity.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 940.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman comes to the physician because she is seeing things that she knows are not there. Sometimes she sees a dog in her kitchen and at other times she sees a stranger in her garden, both of which no one else can see. She also reports a lack of motivation to do daily tasks for the past week. Three years ago, she was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and was started on levodopa and carbidopa. Her younger brother has schizophrenia. The patient also takes levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. She used to drink a bottle of wine every day, but she stopped drinking alcohol 2 months ago. Neurologic examination shows a mild resting tremor of the hands and bradykinesia. Her thought process is organized and logical. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adverse effects of Medication
  • While hallucinations may be caused by dysregulation of a variety of neurotransmitters, this patient's symptoms are most likely due to the activation of dopamine D2-receptors.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 452.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing weakness in his arms and legs over the past year. He has also had difficulty speaking for the past 5 months. He underwent a partial gastrectomy for gastric cancer 10 years ago. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), his pulse is 88/min, and his blood pressure is 118/70 mmHg. Examination shows dysarthria. There is mild atrophy and twitching of the tongue. Muscle strength is decreased in all extremities. Muscle tone is decreased in the right lower extremity and increased in the other extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are absent in the right lower extremity and 4+ in the other extremities. The plantar reflex shows an extensor response on the left. The sensation is intact in all extremities. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Riluzole
  • This man has clinical features of upper motor neuron disease (increased muscle tone, extensor plantar response, and increased DTRs) as well as lower motor neuron disease (decreased muscle tone, atrophy, fasciculations, and absent DTRs), which suggest amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 943.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old hypertensive male has been diagnosed with wide-angle glaucoma when he went for a routine ophthalmological examination. The following drugs can be given as topical eye drops to this patient except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Iloprost
  • Iloprost, a PGI2 analogue produces vasodilatation & is used in the treatment of Pulmonary hypertension. Iloprost has predominant action on the pulmonary artery causing pulmonary vasodilatation and thus is helpful in pulmonary hypertension.
  • It has no effect on uveoscleral outflow. Hence, it is not used in glaucoma.


Goodman & Gilman’s The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 683, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 206

questions.stem: A 63-year-old male came to the casualty with symptoms of shortness of breath, dizziness & tightness in the chest. The doctor diagnosed him with pulmonary hypertension. The following drugs can be given to this patient except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Alprostadil
  • Alprostadil: (PGE1 analogue) is used in the treatment of erectile dysfunction. It is injected into the penis which causes an erection lasting 1–2 hours. However, oral sildenafil/ tadalafil is now preferred. It is also used to maintain patency of ductus arteriosus in neonates with congenital heart defects, till corrective surgery is undertaken. Apnoea occurs in a few cases. It is not used in the treatment of pulmonary hypertension.


Goodman & Gilman’s The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 683, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 207

questions.stem: A 20-year-old primipara woman was admitted to the obstetrical unit for labour induction because of a postdated Pregnancy. Her obstetrical examination was normal, but her Cervix was unfavourable for induction of labour with oxytocin. Which of the following drugs given intravaginally would be appropriately administered at this time?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dinoprostone
  • Prostaglandins E and F are able to terminate a pregnancy at any stage by promoting uterine contractions. They are also able to ripen the cervix (i.e., to make it softer) by increasing Proteoglycan content and changing the biophysical properties of collagen. Dinoprostone, a synthetic prostaglandin E2, is administered intravaginally for ripening of the cervix in pregnant women at or near term whose cervix is not yet soft enough for oxytocin Induction of labour.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 206

questions.stem: A 5-day-old premature male baby, born by normal vaginal Delivery, presented with severe cyanosis. Chest x-rays and Echocardiography confirmed the diagnosis of congenital transposition of the great arteries, and the baby was scheduled for surgery. Which of the following drugs was most likely administered by intravenous infusion to the baby until Surgery?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alprostadil
  • When a baby is born with a congenital heart disease (transposition of the great arteries, pulmonary artery stenosis, etc.), it is important to maintain the patency of the ductus arteriosus before corrective surgery. The patency of the fetal Ductus arteriosus depends primarily on prostaglandin E2 and to a lesser extent on prostaglandin E1. At birth, prostaglandin E1 and E2 levels are reduced because the increased Blood oxygen speeds up prostaglandin metabolism, so the Ductus arteriosus closes in 1 or 2 days. Alprostadil is a synthetic prostaglandin E1 that can maintain the patency of the Ductus arteriosus when given after birth. Because it is metabolized quickly (the half-life is about 10 minutes), it must be given by continuous infusion.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 207

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman recently diagnosed with osteoarthritis started treatment with ibuprofen and misoprostol. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely expected from Misoprostol treatment?
questions.solutionHtml:
Diarrhea
  • Misoprostol is a prostaglandin E1 analogue approved for the Prevention of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug-induced peptic ulcers. Diarrhoea is the most common adverse effect of the drug (up to 30% of patients) and is the main reason for its infrequent clinical use.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 212

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman came to medicine OPD because of progressive exertional dyspnea and arthralgias. Further examination led to the diagnosis of primary pulmonary hypertension, and an intravenous infusion of epoprostenol was started. Which of the following molecular actions most likely mediated the therapeutic efficacy of the drug in the patient’s disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Activation of prostaglandin I2 receptors
  • Epoprostenol is a synthetic prostacyclin (prostaglandin I2) that has powerful vasodilating activity. The drug has been approved for the treatment of primary pulmonary hypertension, a disease of unknown cause involving obliteration of medium and small pulmonary arteries and resulting in right ventricular failure or fatal syncope 2 to 5 years after detection.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 207
